title: When the Hollow Breaks
premise: Tamsin Thornbury, a mercenary and ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, has spent ten years hiding the god-gift she inherited from her mother—until the crown's witch-hunt forces the guild to shelter hunted gift-bearers, and Tamsin discovers her ledgers contain coded proof that the silent god was not dead but imprisoned by the first kings. Hunted by an inquisitor who was once her sworn brother, she must choose between destroying the evidence to keep her guild safe or revealing it to free the god and reignite the ancient war between divine and mortal rule. In the end, Tamsin breaks into the Hollow beneath the capital, frees the god at terrible cost to her guild and her own identity, and forges a fragile new covenant that makes gift-bearers witnesses rather than weapons.
about_author: E. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval trade records before turning to fantasy. They write about ledgers, oaths, and the quiet violence of bureaucracy from a drafty house on the northern coast.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Tamsin audits the guild's strangest accounts—a bottled storm, a borrowed year—establishing her precision and her hidden gift, which she uses only to verify impossible trades. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: controlled contentment built on concealment, with the first hairline crack when a client's payment arrives smeared in royal seal-wax.

chapters.title: A Proclamation in Ash
chapters.summary: Criers announce the Crown's hunt for the god-gifted; a neighbor is taken in broad daylight while Tamsin watches, unable to act without exposing herself. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: fear curdling into guilt—the invisibility she prized becomes complicity.

chapters.title: The Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Oren Vael convenes the partners: they will quietly shelter hunted gift-bearers as 'impossible cargo,' and he assigns Tamsin to forge their papers because her ledgers never lie. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: reluctant loyalty; she agrees, telling herself it's just another entry in the books.

chapters.title: What My Mother Left Me
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: Tamsin opens her mother's sealed strongbox and finds a prayer-token that hums when she holds it—the first sign her gift is inherited, not random. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: grief reopening; inheritance reframed as burden rather than blessing.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Dain Corvasser—Tamsin's childhood sworn brother from the mercenary company—arrives to inspect the guild, all courtesy and veiled threats, clearly suspecting something. POV: alternating Tamsin and Dain. Emotional beat: old affection weaponized; each recognizes the other and both pretend otherwise.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Tamsin smuggles a terrified gifted child, Wren, through the city's tollgates using forged provenance, nearly caught when the girl's gift flares. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose; the abstract hunt gains a face.

chapters.title: Entries in a Dead God's Hand
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing century-old guild ledgers, Tamsin deciphers a cipher her mother used: entries recording payments made by the first kings to 'keep the Hollow shut'—evidence the god was imprisoned, not silent. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: scholarly thrill collapsing into dread as the scale of the secret lands.

chapters.title: Oathbound
chapters.summary: Dain privately warns Tamsin he knows she was marked at birth and offers to falsify her clearance if she surrenders the guild's cargo lists. POV: Dain, with a Tamsin interlude. Emotional beat: betrayal offered as mercy; loyalty and truth pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Partners Vote
chapters.summary: Tamsin reveals the Hollow evidence to the guild partners; Oren argues for burning it, the younger partners for using it, and the vote splits the guild down the middle. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made institutional—her revelation endangers everyone she serves.

chapters.title: Fire in the Ledger Room
chapters.summary: An arsonist destroys half the guild archives; Tamsin saves the cipher pages but loses the originals that could authenticate them, and Wren goes missing in the chaos. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: loss and suspicion—someone inside sold them out.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tamsin traces the arson to partner Selke Marrow, who sold the guild to buy her own family's exemption from the hunt. POV: Selke, then Tamsin confronting her. Emotional beat: pity warring with fury; even betrayal has comprehensible reasons.

chapters.title: Wren in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Tamsin finds Wren hiding with a cell of underground gift-bearers who worship the imprisoned god and believe Tamsin, as token-bearer, is prophesied to free him. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: being seen fully for the first time—and the crushing weight of others' hope.

chapters.title: What the Gift Costs
chapters.summary: The underground shows Tamsin what full use of her gift means: she reads the true history of any object, and the prayer-token shows her the god's imprisonment—his voice screaming inside her skull for one unbearable night. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: horror and awe entangled; ignorance was a kind of mercy.

chapters.title: Corvasser's Net
chapters.summary: Dain arrests the bell tower cell; Wren escapes only because Tamsin burns her own cover to pull her out, making Tamsin officially hunted. POV: alternating Dain and Tamsin. Emotional beat: point of no return; Dain lets her go and hates himself for it.

chapters.title: The Broken Guild
chapters.summary: With the guild raided and Oren dying of wounds taken covering the escape, he gives Tamsin the master key to the guild's oldest vault and names her guildmaster in exile. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: inheritance again—this time chosen; grief fused with resolve.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Dain offers Tamsin a final bargain: the crown will spare the gifted if she delivers the Hollow evidence and renounces her gift publicly. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as peace; Tamsin sees the covenant would just be a quieter prison.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath the River
chapters.summary: Tamsin, Wren, and the surviving loyalists travel the drowned aqueducts toward the capital's foundations, guided by the token, pursued by Selke's information and Dain's soldiers. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: grim fellowship; found-family forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Hollow
chapters.summary: They reach the Hollow: a cathedral-sized prison where the god hangs bound in chains of written law—every oath ever sworn to him turned into his fetters. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: terrible beauty; understanding that loyalty itself became the cage.

chapters.title: Where Loyalty Ends
chapters.summary: Dain corners them at the threshold; Tamsin shows him the god's true history through the gift, forcing him to choose between his crown-oath and the truth. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: catharsis—he breaks his oath, turns his blade against his own inquisitors, and falls buying them time.

chapters.title: When the Hollow Breaks
chapters.summary: Tamsin unbinds the god by releasing every oath sworn to him—including her own mercenary vow—sacrificing her identity as a sworn blade; the god wakes, war erupts in the capital above, and she walks out unnamed. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: climax and cost—freedom purchased with self-erasure.

chapters.title: A New Covenant
chapters.summary: In the smoking aftermath, Tamsin negotiates with the awakened god: no more oaths, only witness—gifted folk as record-keepers of divine truth, guild-ledgers reborn as public law. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: weary triumph; the theme resolved as loyalty rebuilt on truth instead of obedience.

chapters.title: The First Honest Entry
chapters.summary: Epilogue: months later, Tamsin reopens the guild under a new charter with Wren as her apprentice and writes the first entry in a ledger meant to be read by anyone. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: quiet restoration—identity remade not by oath but by choice, ending on an open door.
